title: Understanding Pipe Slope and Gravity Drainage
description: Gravity is the primary driving force behind residential and commercial drainage systems. Because drainage pipes do not operate under pressure like supply lines, maintaining proper horizontal slope is critical to system longevity and performance. If a pipe is pitched too steeply, liquid wastewater rushes away too fast, leaving heavy solid waste behind to accumulate on the pipe bottom. Conversely, if the slope is too shallow, water moves too slowly to transport solids efficiently, frequently resulting in persistent blockages. Professional installation requires adhering strictly to local building codes and manufacturer specifications for continuous, uniform fall across every horizontal drainage run.
